documents.title: Chest tightness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 6 weeks of a tight band across the chest when he walks up the hill on his street or carries groceries up from the car. Goes away within a few minutes of standing still. Never at rest, never woken him. No radiation, no sweating, no fainting. Not getting worse.

Known CAD from 2012 stress test, never cathed. On aspirin and atorvastatin 40.

Exam: BP per flowsheet. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

ECG in office: sinus, no ischemic changes, same as 2017.

A/P: exertional angina in known CAD, stable pattern. Cardiology referral, asked for a visit within 2-3 weeks. Reviewed: call 911 for pain at rest, pain lasting more than 15 min, or with sweating or shortness of breath. Stop smoking - said it plainly again.

reports.text: Bruce protocol. Exercised 5 minutes 40 seconds, reaching 7 METs, 86% of predicted maximal heart rate. Stopped for typical chest tightness. Horizontal ST depression of 2 mm in V2 through V5 beginning at 4 minutes, resolving 5 minutes into recovery. No arrhythmia. Blood pressure response normal.
reports.conclusion: Positive exercise test for ischemia in the anterior leads with reproduction of angina.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for referring Mr. Dabrowski, 70, seen 6/14/2022 for six weeks of exertional chest tightness. History of CAD by stress testing in 2012, medically managed. Diabetes, CKD stage 4, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, active smoker with 40 pack-years.

Exam: regular rhythm, no murmur or gallop, lungs clear, no edema.

Treadmill test today reproduced his angina at moderate workload with 2 mm ST depression in the anterior leads.

Assessment: stable angina with anterior ischemia.

Plan: coronary angiography with possible intervention, using minimal contrast and pre- and post-procedure IV fluids given his kidney function, coordinated with his nephrologist. Continue aspirin and atorvastatin. Smoking cessation strongly advised.

NKDA.

Cardiology

medications.sig: Dissolve 1 tablet under the tongue every 5 minutes as needed for chest pain, up to 3

reports.text: Right radial access. Left main normal. LAD: 90% proximal stenosis. Circumflex: mild luminal irregularities. Right coronary: 40% mid-vessel narrowing. Left ventricular function not assessed by ventriculography to limit contrast. Intervention: proximal LAD treated with a single drug-eluting stent, 3.0 x 18 mm, 0% residual, TIMI 3 flow. Contrast 45 mL.
reports.conclusion: Single-vessel intervention: drug-eluting stent to the proximal LAD. Moderate RCA disease for medical therapy.

documents.title: Catheterization and discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Elective coronary angiography 8/19/2022 for angina with a positive stress test. Proximal LAD 90% stenosis treated with one drug-eluting stent via the right radial artery. RCA 40% and mild circumflex disease left for medical therapy. Kept overnight for IV fluids; creatinine unchanged the next morning. Radial site without hematoma.

New medications: clopidogrel 75 mg daily with aspirin 81 mg daily, uninterrupted for at least 12 months - do not stop without speaking to cardiology. Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg under the tongue as needed for chest pain.
Continue: insulin glargine, lisinopril 10 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, sevelamer, calcitriol, darbepoetin per nephrology, acetaminophen as needed.

Referred to cardiac rehab. Clinic follow-up in 3 months.

Cardiology

conditions.label: Acute ST elevation myocardial infarction of inferior wall

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 92. ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 12/23/2022.

70 y/o man with diabetes, stage 4 CKD and CAD (LAD drug-eluting stent in August) brought by ambulance with severe chest pain into the left arm, began 30 minutes before arrival while sitting at home. He tells us he stopped all of his pills about a week ago because he was feeling well and the costs were adding up.

On arrival BP 160/90, sweaty and visibly distressed.

ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF with reciprocal changes - STEMI activation.
Labs: troponin I 12 ng/mL (normal under 0.04), CK-MB 80 U/L (0-24), myoglobin 1500 ng/mL (28-72).

Given aspirin 325 mg chewed, clopidogrel load, heparin per protocol. Taken directly to the cath lab.

Disposition: admitted to cardiology after catheterization.

NKDA.

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 25 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet

reports.text: Emergent angiography, right radial access. Right coronary: thrombotic total occlusion of the mid vessel. LAD: previously placed proximal stent widely patent, no restenosis. Circumflex: mild irregularities. Intervention: a single drug-eluting stent to the mid RCA, 3.5 x 22 mm, TIMI 3 flow restored. Contrast 70 mL.
reports.conclusion: Inferior STEMI from mid-RCA occlusion, treated with a drug-eluting stent. Patent LAD stent.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size with hypokinesis of the inferior wall. Estimated ejection fraction 45%. Right ventricle normal in size and function. No significant valve disease. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Mildly reduced LV function, EF 45%, with inferior hypokinesis.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admitted 12/23/2022, discharged 12/27/2022.

Diagnosis: acute inferior ST-elevation MI from occlusion of the mid right coronary artery.

Course: emergent catheterization from the ED showed a thrombotic mid-RCA occlusion, treated with a drug-eluting stent. The LAD stent from August was patent. Pain resolved after reperfusion. No arrhythmia on telemetry. Echo 12/24: EF 45% with inferior hypokinesis. Creatinine rose to 3.6 after contrast and came back to 3.2 by discharge with fluids. He had stopped all medications a week before admission because of cost and feeling well; we went through why each one matters, especially clopidogrel and aspirin with two stents, and social work linked him with a drug assistance program.

He decided to quit smoking and stop drinking; he has not smoked since admission.

Discharge medications:
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- clopidogrel 75 mg daily (12 months from this event; do not interrupt)
- metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily - NEW
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime
- sevelamer carbonate 800 mg three times daily with meals
- calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily
- darbepoetin per nephrology
- nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual as needed
- acetaminophen as needed
NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within a week; cardiology 4-6 weeks; cardiac rehab re-referral.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call after discharge 12/27 for heart attack. Pt home, daughter staying with him this week. No chest pain, no shortness of breath. Has picked up all discharge meds; the assistance program covered the clopidogrel. Taking every pill, daughter set up a weekly pillbox. No cigarettes since 12/23. Appt with PCP 1/4 confirmed. ED record received today and routed.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with daughter, 8 days after discharge for an inferior STEMI (mid RCA occlusion, DES; LAD stent from August patent). EF 45% with inferior hypokinesis. He had stopped all his meds the week before for cost. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed.

Since home: no chest pain, walking in the house and to the mailbox, a little tired. Every med in the pillbox, assistance program covering clopidogrel. Has not smoked since 12/23 and has not had a drink. Proud of it, and he should be.

Meds reconciled: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25 (new), atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 10, glargine 24 qhs, sevelamer 800 tid, calcitriol 0.25, darbepoetin q4 wk (nephrology), SL NTG prn, acetaminophen prn.

Exam: BP and HR per flowsheet. R wrist site healed. Heart regular, no murmur, no gallop. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Inferior STEMI s/p RCA DES; prior LAD DES - DAPT uninterrupted, metoprolol. Cardiology 4-6 weeks, rehab re-referral placed by hospital. Talked through costs and that he must call us before stopping anything; we can find a cheaper option every time.
2. Tobacco - quit 12/23. Former smoker. Offered patch for cravings; he says he doesn't need it.
3. CKD 4 - creatinine bumped with contrast, BMP today.
4. DM2 - glargine unchanged.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Seen 2/14/2023 for follow-up after his December inferior STEMI with RCA stent; LAD stent August 2022. No angina, no dyspnea. Cardiac rehab started this month. Off cigarettes since admission.

Blood pressure and heart rate at goal on metoprolol. Regular rhythm, no gallop, lungs clear, no edema.

Plan: continue aspirin and clopidogrel through December 2023, metoprolol succinate 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, lisinopril 10 mg. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Plavix
documents.author: patient
documents.body: It's almost a year since the heart attack. Do I stop the clopidogrel now or wait for the heart doctor? I don't want to mess it up again.

documents.title: RE: Plavix
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question, and thank you for asking first. Keep taking it until cardiology tells you to stop. Your appointment with them is in early January and that's when they planned to make the change. Keep the aspirin no matter what.
